title: Methods choices in test-negative influenza vaccine effectiveness studies: a scoping review
abstract: Objective: to map how test-negative studies of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness handled case definition, test type, specimen timing, calendar time, repeat testing, prior vaccination, vaccination source and SARS-CoV-2-positive controls. Design: scoping review following JBI methods, reported with PRISMA-ScR. Results will follow charting.
introduction: Published estimates vary widely, and methods choices plausibly explain part of the variation. The last survey of reporting covered studies to 2018.
methods: Registered protocol; library searches of four databases and two preprint servers; double screening of 20 percent; a piloted charting form; descriptive mapping by period.
results: No data have been charted yet. The report will present the flow of studies and a heat map of methods choices by period.
discussion: The discussion will translate the map into the regional protocol's choices; the evidence on test type will be re-checked after the correction of a cited record's publication year.
limitations: Reporting is not practice; coverage of databases and languages.
conclusion: To be written after charting; it will not estimate vaccine effectiveness.
summary: PRISMA-ScR structured draft with results left empty.
